title: FortiGuard Labs: fake delivery notices, stolen logins and malicious domains target holiday shoppers
date_note: The Fortinet blog post is dated 24 Nov 2026; no earlier day given.
summary: FortiGuard Labs reports newly registered holiday-related domains, some classified as malicious, with parcel and delivery terms common among them. Lookalike domains imitate USPS, UPS, FedEx and DHL, often asking for small redelivery fees or personal data. The post also describes infostealer logs tied to e-commerce platforms and an unverified underground seller claim of access to OpenCart storefronts.
plain: Fortinet's researchers say scam websites posing as delivery firms and stolen shopping-account logins are being used against holiday shoppers.
exec: Per FortiGuard Labs, retailers face lookalike delivery domains, stolen customer logins and a claimed storefront-access sale.
action: FortiGuard Labs advises monitoring lookalike domains, blocking verified malicious domains, watching for failed-login spikes and card testing, and alerting on unexpected checkout-script changes.

sources.name: Fortinet blog: Fake Delivery Notices, Stolen Logins, and Malicious Domains

validation.note: Fortinet's own research post read; the OpenCart access claim is a seller's claim the post does not verify.

review.note: compared summary, claim wording and advice with the Fortinet post
